text: The Army awarded the contract for Camp East Montana at Fort Bliss, Texas, worth up to $1.3 billion, and handed it to ICE in October 2025. It opened in August 2025 as ICE's largest detention site.

GAO found the Army paid full price for guards, meals and other services from August 1 to 15, 2025, before anyone was held there, wasting up to $11.5 million. In March 2026 ICE ended the contract and chose a new contractor.

Guantánamo: the Defense Department obligated about $68 million for immigration detention from October 2024 to May 2026, and ICE about $43 million from October 2024 to June 2026. An average of 16 people were held there in fiscal year 2026 (through June 18). Putting up tents that were never used cost $2.85 million.
The Defense Department moved $1.74 billion of its 2025 funds to its southern border mission and began spending from $1 billion given in the July 2025 budget law.

A report by Democratic members of Congress counts at least $2 billion of Defense money committed to immigration enforcement in 2025, including $420.9 million for detention on military bases and $40.3 million for flights on military aircraft.
source: Sen. Warren and Rep. Garamendi, cost report

text: The immigration courts had 3,666,795 pending cases at the end of December 2025, down from 3,925,499 at the end of fiscal year 2024.
source: Justice Department, EOIR budget request for fiscal year 2027

text: Immigration court budget: $844 million in fiscal year 2025 and $800 million in 2026; $899 million requested for 2027.
source: Justice Department, EOIR budget request for fiscal year 2027

text: ICE and the Bureau of Prisons signed an agreement in February 2025 to hold people in federal prisons; it now runs to July 2027. In fiscal year 2026 an average of 1,126 people were held across eight federal prisons, at a median $182 a day each, about double ICE's median of $92.
ICE also holds people as a "rider" on U.S. Marshals Service contracts and agreements.

FEMA gave Florida $608.4 million on September 30, 2025 under its Detention Support Grant Program, for the Florida Soft-Sided Facility in the Everglades. The grant pays $249 per person per day, 171% more than ICE's median of $92.
According to FEMA, the money came from funds meant for shelters to relieve crowding in CBP holding facilities.

The Everglades site held 1,386 people on average in fiscal year 2026 (through April) and closed in June 2026. Baker Correctional Institution in Florida also holds ICE detainees without an ICE contract (959 on average in fiscal year 2026); FEMA says it will be reimbursed at the same $249 a day.

From 2019 through 2024 CBP obligated over $4 billion for tent-like soft-sided holding facilities and their services. It stopped running them in March 2025, except that the El Paso site kept operating under a new Army contract for ICE.
In 2020 GAO found 31 deaths in CBP custody on the southwest border in fiscal years 2014 to 2019, of which CBP could show it had reported only 20 to Congress.
